body.statement: Can the priors obtained from \(\mathrm{def:common-marginal-prior-handle}\) be normalized and transferred to the fixed two-sample experiment so that they induce identical auxiliary laws and imply \[R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\ge c_\epsilon r_\epsilon(n,m,d)\] for every \(n\ge1\), \(m\ge0\), and \(d\ge2\), including the capped constant-risk regime?
body.justification: A supervised lower prior that perturbs \(P_{XA}\) is detected by the auxiliary sample, so exact marginal invariance is the essential new converse mechanism.
body.gap: ZengBalakrishnanHanKennedy2024, Appendix C.5, randomizes treatment and mass parameters in a one-sample fuzzy hypothesis; WuYang2016 provides approximation duality but not the auxiliary-invariance constraint or the two-sample normalization transfer. The two point masses in \(\mathrm{def:finite-small-instance}\) verify exact \(P_{XA}\) agreement and label-gated discrepancy in a finite experiment, but their total variation is too large to supply the all-regime frontier.
body.consumer: The lower bound prevents chart-review planning from treating unlabeled records as if they also supplied outcome-bearing moments.

obligation.what_is_open: An explicit normalized pair of fuzzy priors that keeps the entire random \(P_{XA}\) identical, survives transfer to fixed sample sizes, and produces the dimension-dependent and capped lower-bound terms in every regime.
obligation.obstruction: The frozen prior handle does not define the moment-matching measures, reservoir normalization, or likelihood comparison. The finite two-point construction preserves \(P_{XA}\) but its separation is only parametric when its labeled likelihoods are kept close, so it cannot certify the conjectured dimension-dependent frontier.
obligation.attempted: A same-marginal two-point subexperiment was analyzed exactly using its chi-squared product likelihood. It closes the universal \(n^{-1}\) lower bound, but scaling the outcome perturbation to constant separation makes the labeled product laws distinguishable and does not implement the required approximation-dual fuzzy prior.
obligation.partial_result: The two-point family \(P_-\), \(P_+\) used in \(\texttt{thm:known-marginal-boundary}\) has identical \(P_{XA}\), target separation \(1/(8\sqrt n)\), and labeled-sample total variation below \(1/2\).  Therefore it also yields the dimension-free lower bound \(R_\epsilon(n,m,d)\geq1/(512n)\) for every finite \(m\), because the auxiliary laws agree exactly.  It does not yield the dimension-dependent part or the capped constant-risk regime of the proposed frontier.
